title: Simultaneous generic flatness of an algebra and a finite module
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain, $B$ a commutative finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $M$ a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There exists $0\ne a\in A$ such that both $B_a=B[1/\varphi(a)]$ and $M_a=M[1/\varphi(a)]$ are flat as $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], where $\varphi:A\to B$ is the structure map. The localizations are at the powers of $\varphi(a)$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and their $A$-module structures are induced by $A\to B\to B_a$. Neither $A$ being Noetherian nor $B$ or $M$ being finitely presented is required.

source.place: Tag 051T, lemma-generic-flatness, conclusion (a), applied in Tag 0573, lemma-scheme-theoretically-dense-generic-fibre, proof third paragraph; square-zero specialization of the algebra case.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $A$ and module generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ of $M$ over $B$. Form the commutative square-zero algebra $C=B\oplus M$ of [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], with structure map $u\mapsto(\varphi(u),0)$. It is generated over $A$ by the finitely many $(b_i,0)$ and $(0,m_j)$: for $(b,m)\in C$, write $b=P(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ and $m=\sum_j c_jm_j$ with $c_j=P_j(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$; then $(b,m)=P((b_i,0))+\sum_j P_j((b_i,0))(0,m_j)$. Thus the defining finite-generation criterion makes $C$ finite type over $A$.

source.place: Tag 051T, lemma-generic-flatness, conclusion (a); agent-written square-zero reduction to the existing algebra-only theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-finite-type-algebra-generic-flatness] to $A\to C$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is a domain, $C$ is commutative, and step 1 proves finite type. Obtain $a\ne0$ in $A$ such that $F=C[1/t]$, where $s=\varphi(a)$ and $t=(s,0)$, is flat over $A$: take this particular localization as the theorem's arbitrary localization model. Flatness of the composite ring map is precisely flatness of the underlying $A$-module $F$ by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 051T, lemma-generic-flatness, conclusion (a); agent-written square-zero reduction to the existing algebra-only theorem.

proof.text: Construct $A$-linear maps $i_B:B_s\to F$, $p_B:F\to B_s$, $i_M:M_s\to F$, and $p_M:F\to M_s$ by $i_B(b/s^e)=(b,0)/t^e$, $i_M(m/s^e)=(0,m)/t^e$, $p_B((b,m)/t^e)=b/s^e$, and $p_M((b,m)/t^e)=m/s^e$. These are well-defined directly by the fraction relations: equality of $(b,m)/t^e$ and $(b\prime,m\prime)/t^{e\prime}$ means that for some $k\ge0$ both $s^k(s^{e\prime}b-s^eb\prime)=0$ and $s^k(s^{e\prime}m-s^em\prime)=0$, since $t^j=(s^j,0)$. This implies equality of both projected fractions. Conversely an equality of $B_s$-fractions or $M_s$-fractions gives the required equality after its inclusion, the other coordinate being zero. The fraction addition formulas show additivity of all four maps, and multiplication by $(\varphi(u),0)$ shows $A$-linearity for $u\in A$. On every fraction $p_Bi_B$ and $p_Mi_M$ are the identity. Hence both specified localizations $B_s$ and $M_s$ are $A$-module retracts of $F$.

source.place: Tag 051T, lemma-generic-flatness, conclusion (a); agent-written square-zero reduction to the existing algebra-only theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract] twice, to $(i_B,p_B)$ and $(i_M,p_M)$ of step 3, with ambient flat $A$-module $F$ from step 2. It yields flatness over $A$ of $B_s=B_a$ and $M_s=M_a$ for the same nonzero $a$. Their scalar actions are the stipulated ones because all four maps use $u\mapsto(\varphi(u),0)$ and componentwise scalar multiplication. This proves every clause without any Noetherianity or finite-presentation hypothesis.
